doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Conducting Basie's band and playing at Basie's birthday party
summary: Touring England with Basie behind Bennett led to playing piano for Basie's birthday at the Waldorf.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. I even took his place at his birthday party one time. That was another thrill for me.

Yeah. At the Waldorf Astoria, at the Grand Ballroom, they had a big birthday party, I think it was his 65th or 70th, I don’t know 65th I guess. And I had been, we had just made a little tour. I mean I was still playing with Tony Bennett was my regular job. And we had just finished a tour of England with Count Basie’s band backing up Tony Bennett and also doing their own music. And the guys kind of liked me. I used to travel on the bus. I preferred traveling on the bus with them, to riding in a limo with Tony. Not that I was trying to be down home, I just, to tell you the truth, for personal, I wanted to stay

away from Tony Bennett. I got so much of Tony Bennett and hearing him complain to the agent about the business and this and that, and so I liked going with the guys in the band. So anyhow, as a result of the band having confidence in me, they hired me to play at his birthday party with Basie’s band up on the stage. So that was a great kick for me. And I grew up, you know, listening to Basie. They even used to call me “Count Bunch” when I was about fourteen, fifteen years old, because I could imitate him too you know. So I mean you know all these years passed and then here I am sitting playing old Basie’s music. It was a big thrill.

Yeah, in front of Basie. And Basie was there and Jo Jones and all the many of his ex- musicians. Buck Clayton was in the audience and oh, it was an unbelievable experience. I just ran into a couple of the guys who remembered that. A couple of the Basie guys who are still with him — Mel — I can’t remember the trombone player’s name, been with them all these twenty something years. We were talking about that experience.
